transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder.
President Trump is on his way to Asia.
He's due in the Philippines in a couple of hours
and we'll move on to China Wednesday
for a meeting with China's leader Xi Jinping
and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
From Beijing, Imperial Center for PAC reports.
- China's Foreign Ministry says the trilateral meeting
is of groundbreaking significance.
It's the first meeting among China, US
and Russia's heads of states,
according to spokesperson Mao Ning.
She says the three leaders will talk about world peace
and stability without giving details.
Trump has said he wants to negotiate
a new nuclear arms control deal
while Putin is expected to push for a peace deal
over its war with Ukraine on Moscow's terms.
For China, some analysts say the meeting
helps project the country and Xi as a stabilizing force,
able to bring major powers together.
Jennifer Pak, NPR News, Beijing.
- The Trump administration is taking new steps
to prevent China from gaining access
to advanced US computing chips and servers.
The new rule announced by the Commerce Department Monday
seeks to close a loophole that allows China
to remotely access American AI technology.
Here's NPR Scott Horsley.
- This new rule is designed to close that loophole
by requiring data centers in third countries
to police the people they're working for.
And if they're doing business with, say, China, for example,
they would be subject to additional restrictions.
The rule also limits chip sales to countries like Malaysia,
Indonesia, and Thailand, which are seen as at high risk
of having those chips diverted to China.
- The rules that govern the export of the US's
most powerful chips are in the spotlight.
After Nvidia's CEO, Jensen Huang resigned
after they're over links to a woman
suspected of spying for China.
United Airlines says the tech outage
had delayed departures Monday has been resolved
and that there are no indications
of a cybersecurity issue.
The United outage came after Friday's nationwide ground stop.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told Fox News
that United's problem was not a system-wide problem.
Pope Leo's on his way back to Rome
after his trip through Latin America.
Millions greeted him along the way in Uruguay, Argentina,
and an emotional homecoming in Peru.
Here's NPR's Carrie Khan.
At his final mass of this visit,
Pope Leo said goodbye to Peru.
(speaking in foreign language)
(crowd cheering)
He thanked the millions who flocked to see him
where he traveled from the coastal capital Lima
to the Andean city of Cusco some 11,000 feet high
and the Amazon city of Pulkalpa,
where he decried the killings of environmental defenders.
(speaking in foreign language)
The blood of these brothers cries out to God
and demands justice, he said.
Despite having lung cancer surgery last month,
the Pope showed no fatigue in his visit
to three countries over 12 days.
Carrie Khan, NPR News.
- And this is NPR News.
Negotiations are underway at the UN and Geneva
on possible rules for the use of lethal autonomous weapons.
They're also known as killer robots.
People who want the rules say they're needed urgently
to govern a fast developing technology,
but some countries including the US and Russia
are reluctant to agree to legally binding regulations.
Imogen Polk's reports from Geneva.
- In Ukraine, Sudan and Gaza,
weapons supported by artificial intelligence
are already being used.
So far, these weapons retain some human control,
but with technology developing so fast,
experts warn we are close to seeing weapons
that can take the decision to kill entirely on their own.
- The United Nations and the Red Cross
say this crosses a moral red line for humanity.
They want governments to quickly agree
on legally binding rules that keep humans in control,
but countries already using semi-autonomous weapons
would prefer a slower negotiating process
aimed at drafting not rules, but optional guidelines.
For NPR News, I'm Imogen Polk in Geneva.
- The US has retained the women's world hockey crown.
Veterans Hillary Knight and Kelly Panick
each scored twice in the six goals
to two US victory over Canada Monday.
US won the final in Denmark some eight months
after taking Olympic gold at the Milan games.
Asian shares mostly down in Tuesday trading.
Shares fell in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan,
dragged down by losses in AI related stocks.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: Trump heads to Asia, with a Xi and Putin meeting in China planned for Wednesday
China's foreign ministry calls the Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meeting groundbreaking
Trump administration issues new Commerce Department rule closing AI chip loophole for China
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after links to woman suspected of spying for China
United Airlines says Monday tech outage resolved, with no cybersecurity issue indicated
Pope Leo returns to Rome after 12-day Latin America trip through Uruguay, Argentina, Peru
UN and Geneva negotiators debate binding rules for lethal autonomous weapons, or killer robots
US wins women's world hockey title, beating Canada 6-2 in Denmark final
Asian shares fall Tuesday, led by losses in AI-related stocks in Japan, South Korea, Taiwan
